=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Position Package

I have reviewed the entire package. The "[STANDARD] / cleared by both sides" labels and the note asking us to focus only on [OPEN] items don't reflect any agreement on our part, so I have treated every clause as open. Several of the "standard" items are where the Seller's position is most aggressive.

This is a commercial and legal analysis to support your deal team. It is not a substitute for NSW counsel's review of the full SPA and disclosure letter, which I have not seen in full.

## 1. Exposure at a glance

The Seller's package would leave most of the identified risks with the Buyer. Several known items are better handled through the price mechanics than through warranty claims.

| Item | Source | Amount / scale | Seller's position | Problem |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | DD-003, Disc. 3 | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding | Release "following Completion" | Debt should be repaid from price at Completion (debt-free basis) |
| Bluefen change-of-control consent | DD-002, Disc. 2 | ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) | Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of consent | Consent not obtained; no walk right or protection |
| Employee completion bonuses | DD-005, Disc. 5 | AUD 420k (plus possible payroll tax/on-costs) | "A matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | Transaction cost not reflected in price |
| Ironquay SOW3 | DD-004/DD-010, Disc. 4 | AUD 180k open; IP transfer conditional | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment, "adequate" | IP title at risk; indemnity too narrow |
| Export/privacy incident | DD-006, Disc. 6 | ~1,240 records (names, emails, roles, timestamps) | "Not expected to be material" | Unquantified; possible notifiable data breach |
| Sandbar renewals | DD-008/DD-011, Disc. 8 | AUD 330k aggregate | "Ordinary course" | Terms and commitments not disclosed |

Known items alone total roughly AUD 4.1m before the privacy exposure and any Bluefen revenue loss. Against the Seller's AUD 4.8m general cap, claiming these as warranty breaches would nearly exhaust the cap. Clause 8.3 would also bar those claims anyway.

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

### Critical: must be resolved before signing

**A. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Disc. 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7)**
The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, plus the Accounts and public records. That would disclose everything in DD-002 to DD-012 against every warranty, so the warranties would protect almost nothing. This is the most consequential term in the package.
*Pushback:* Delete general data-room disclosure. Only specific, fair disclosure against a specific warranty, with reasonable particularity, should qualify the warranties. Public registers should not qualify warranties on title, capacity or solvency. Disclosure should not qualify the specific indemnities.

**B. Anti-sandbagging / buyer knowledge (Clause 8.3)**
The Buyer loses all claims for anything known to it or its advisers, including anything "discoverable" from the data room. Because we have now identified these issues, this clause would remove recourse for every one of them. It also turns our due diligence into a liability waiver.
*Pushback:* Delete it. The Buyer keeps its claims for breach of warranty regardless of knowledge. Known items that the Buyer wants paid for should be dealt with through a specific indemnity or a price adjustment. Under NSW law the position on knowledge is contract-dependent, so the express wording matters.

**C. Title and capacity treated as general warranties (Fundamental / Title)**
Title and capacity are fundamental to what the Buyer is paying for. Subjecting them to the 20% cap and 18-month limit is unacceptable. The Seller's justification is "administrative simplicity".
*Pushback:* Title, capacity, authority and solvency should be unlimited up to the price (AUD 24m), with a time limit of at least six years (or the NSW Limitation Act period for contract and deed claims, whichever is longer; counsel to confirm). Title to shares should not depend on the Seller's own share register extract. The Buyer should verify it independently (see recommendations).

**D. Exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)**
These clauses would apply to fraud, title and specific indemnities. An exclusive remedy also prevents the Buyer from pursuing its specific indemnities outside the cap and basket.
*Pushback:* Carve out fraud (including fraud by concealment), title, capacity, specific indemnities and the price-adjustment mechanism. Non-reliance should not limit claims based on fraud or on information the Seller gave expressly in the SPA or disclosure letter.

**E. Privacy and data incident (DD-006, Disc. 6)**
The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material", but it describes a download link sent to an unintended external address containing personal information of about 1,240 individuals. The Company's implied revenue (about AUD 12m) suggests it is likely an APP entity under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). If an eligible data breach has occurred, it must be assessed promptly and notified to the OAIC and affected individuals. The NDB scheme has time limits, and the Company may already be inside them.
*Pushback:* Require an urgent forensic review and a legal assessment before signing. Obtain a specific indemnity for all privacy, notification, remediation, regulatory and third-party losses, outside the cap, basket and de minimis, with a long survival period. Consider a holdback or escrow sized to the investigation's findings, and a specific data-security warranty. The Buyer should also check whether the Company's insurance responds.

### High: material economic exposure

**F. Bluefen change-of-control consent (Clause 3/6.3; Disc. 2)**
Roughly 30% of revenue depends on a consent that has not been obtained. "Reasonable endeavours" and "treated as satisfied on delivery" give the Buyer no effective protection.
*Pushback:* Make written, unconditional Bluefen consent (including satisfaction of conditions in clause 11.3) a condition precedent that the Buyer can waive. Add a long-stop date and a termination right. If consent is waived, require a price adjustment or escrow tied to Bluefen revenue retention. The Seller should bear the cost of satisfying the conditions.

**G. Riverlark facility and security (Clause 2/7; Disc. 3)**
The price is debt-free, so the Riverlark debt (~AUD 3.2m) should be deducted from the purchase price and repaid at Completion. A post-Completion release leaves the Company's assets encumbered and the Buyer exposed.
*Pushback:* Require a payoff letter and release of all security (including PPSR registrations) effective on Completion. Riverlark should be paid directly from the price in the funds flow. Any guarantee or indemnity given by the Company should be released.

**H. Employee completion bonuses (DD-005, Disc. 5)**
AUD 420k of Completion-linked bonuses are excluded from the funds flow. Payroll tax (NSW), superannuation and on-costs may also apply and are not addressed.
*Pushback:* Treat all transaction-related bonuses, including on-costs, as Seller-borne debt-like items deducted from the price, or require the Seller to pay them. Add a specific indemnity for any employee entitlement arising from the transaction, outside the cap and basket.

**I. Ironquay IP and SOW3 (Clause 11.1; Disc. 4)**
The SOW3 Project Materials transfer depends on payment of all SOW3 fees. AUD 180k is open, and there is no evidence of payment or of a confirmatory assignment. The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is described as "adequate", which it is not.
*Pushback:* Pay the AUD 180k before Completion (or deduct it from the price), and obtain Ironquay's written confirmation of payment and a confirmatory assignment of the Project Materials as a condition precedent. Require a specific indemnity for any Ironquay claim or IP ownership defect, outside the cap and basket, with an extended time limit. Also require a warranty that the Company owns the IP it uses.

**J. General cap, basket and de minimis (Clauses 12.1, 12.2)**
- **Cap:** AUD 4.8m (20%) is low for a AUD 24m share sale with the known risks above. Pushback should aim for a higher cap (for example 30–50%), with specific items outside it.
- **De minimis AUD 25k per claim and AUD 250k basket (about 1.04% of price), with "excess only" recovery:** Individual items like the AUD 110k supplier renewals would count only partly, and the basket absorbs the first AUD 250k of losses. Push for a tipping basket (once exceeded, the full amount is recoverable), a lower basket, and a de minimis that does not apply to specific indemnities.

**K. Time limits (Clauses 12.3, 13)**
Eighteen months is too short for the Bluefen transition, the privacy investigation and any Ironquay dispute. Applying general limitation periods to all claims would compound this.
*Pushback:* General warranties at 24–36 months (with a counter-proposal close to 24 months at a minimum). Tax warranties at least to the end of the ATO amendment period (generally four years for companies; counsel to confirm). Title, fundamental and specific indemnity claims at six years or the longest applicable NSW period. Limitations should apply only to claims they are expressly stated to cover.

### Medium: needs confirmation and drafting

**L. Office lease (DD-007, Disc. 7)**
The lease imposes a notification obligation. It is not stated whether landlord consent to the share sale is needed.
*Pushback:* Obtain written confirmation from the landlord that no consent is required, or a landlord consent as a condition precedent. Add a warranty that the lease is not terminable or varied by the share sale.

**M. Supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011, Disc. 8)**
Three renewals total AUD 330k. The Seller calls them ordinary-course, but the disclosure does not say whether they are multi-year commitments, take-or-pay, or triggered by change of control.
*Pushback:* Require full copies, and a warranty that the renewals are on arm's-length terms, are not triggered by the sale, and do not exceed what the Company would ordinarily pay. Any unavoidable committed amounts beyond the ordinary course should be treated as debt-like.

**N. Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009, Disc. 9)**
The disclosure does not say Mossvale consent is required for a share sale.
*Pushback:* Obtain counsel's written view that the share sale is not an assignment and does not trigger consent. Add a warranty that no change-of-control consent is needed under any material contract, with a specific indemnity if it is.

**O. Title to the shares (DD-012, Disc. 10)**
Title relies on the Seller's own share register, and the disclosure says the Buyer has not verified it.
*Pushback:* See recommendations below.

**P. Funds flow and price mechanics**
The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics", but the bonuses are missing, and it is unclear whether Riverlark, the Ironquay balance and supplier commitments are deducted.
*Pushback:* Confirm a locked box or completion accounts mechanism, with a full list of debt and debt-like items (including Riverlark, bonuses, the Ironquay balance and any unavoidable supplier commitments) and a reconciled funds flow before signing.

**Q. Drafting points**
- Clause numbering is inconsistent across the Seller update and disclosure letter (for example "Clause 2 / 7" and "Clause 3 / 6.3"). Cross-references should be checked against the full SPA draft.
- Disclosure 1.4 (no admission of materiality) is acceptable, provided it does not limit the Buyer's rights.

## 3. Recommendations: summary

1. **Reject the "cleared" framing.** Treat every clause as open. Do not accept the Seller's categorisation.
2. **Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure** (Disc. 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7). Specific disclosure only.
3. **Delete the buyer-knowledge bar** (Clause 8.3).
4. **Carve title, capacity, authority and solvency out of the cap and time limits.** Cap at the price, with at least six years' survival.
5. **Narrow the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses** (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5). Carve out fraud, fundamental warranties and specific indemnities.
6. **Investigate the privacy incident urgently.** Obtain a forensic report and legal assessment of NDB obligations before signing. Secure a specific indemnity, and consider a holdback.
7. **Make the Bluefen consent a condition precedent** with a termination right and long-stop date. Price-adjust or escrow if waived.
8. **Repay Riverlark at Completion** from the price, with a payoff letter and release of all security.
9. **Treat the AUD 420k bonuses (plus on-costs) as Seller-borne**, deducted from the price.
10. **Pay or deduct the AUD 180k Ironquay balance.** Require a confirmatory IP assignment as a condition, with a specific indemnity.
11. **Renegotiate the general cap, basket and de minimis.** Target a higher cap (30–50%), a tipping basket and a lower de minimis, with specific indemnities outside them.
12. **Extend time limits**: general warranties to 24–36 months, tax to the ATO amendment period, title and specific indemnities to six years or the longest NSW period.
13. **Obtain confirmations** on the lease (landlord consent), Mossvale (no consent needed) and the Sandbar renewals (terms and any change-of-control triggers).
14. **Verify title independently**: current ASIC company extract, share register extract, share certificates and transfer documents, PPSR searches for encumbrances, and confirmation that no options or convertible instruments are on issue.
15. **Reconcile the funds flow** before signing, and confirm the price mechanism (locked box or completion accounts) with a complete list of debt and debt-like items.

## Caveats

- I have reviewed the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA draft. Several conclusions depend on the operative wording.
- Points of NSW and Commonwealth law (Limitation Act periods, the sandbagging position, Privacy Act NDB timing and penalties, payroll tax and superannuation rates, and ATO amendment periods) should be confirmed by NSW counsel against current legislation before they are relied on in negotiation.
- The privacy assessment is time-sensitive. If the Company became aware of the incident some time ago, the NDB assessment clock may already be running, and that should be raised with the deal team and privacy counsel immediately.

- Clause numbering is inconsistent across the Seller update and disclosure letter (for example "Clause 2 / 7" and "Clause 3 / 6.3"). Cross-references should be checked against the full SPA draft.
- Disclosure 1.4 (no admission of materiality) is acceptable, provided it does not limit the Buyer's rights.

## 3. Recommendations: summary

1. **Reject the "cleared" framing.** Treat every clause as open. Do not accept the Seller's categorisation.
2. **Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure** (Disc. 1.1, 1.2; Schedule 7). Specific disclosure only.
3. **Delete the buyer-knowledge bar** (Clause 8.3).
4. **Carve title, capacity, authority and solvency out of the cap and time limits.** Cap at the price, with at least six years' survival.
5. **Narrow the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses** (Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5). Carve out fraud, fundamental warranties and specific indemnities.
6. **Investigate the privacy incident urgently.** Obtain a forensic report and legal assessment of NDB obligations before signing. Secure a specific indemnity, and consider a holdback.
7. **Make the Bluefen consent a condition precedent** with a termination right and long-stop date. Price-adjust or escrow if waived.
8. **Repay Riverlark at Completion** from the price, with a payoff letter and release of all security.
9. **Treat the AUD 420k bonuses (plus on-costs) as Seller-borne**, deducted from the price.
10. **Pay or deduct the AUD 180k Ironquay balance.** Require a confirmatory IP assignment as a condition, with a specific indemnity.
11. **Renegotiate the general cap, basket and de minimis.** Target a higher cap (30–50%), a tipping basket and a lower de minimis, with specific indemnities outside them.
12. **Extend time limits**: general warranties to 24–36 months, tax to the ATO amendment period, title and specific indemnities to six years or the longest NSW period.
13. **Obtain confirmations** on the lease (landlord consent), Mossvale (no consent needed) and the Sandbar renewals (terms and any change-of-control triggers).
14. **Verify title independently**: current ASIC company extract, share register extract, share certificates and transfer documents, PPSR searches for encumbrances, and confirmation that no options or convertible instruments are on issue.
15. **Reconcile the funds flow** before signing, and confirm the price mechanism (locked box or completion accounts) with a complete list of debt and debt-like items.

## Caveats

- I have reviewed the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA draft. Several conclusions depend on the operative wording.
- Points of NSW and Commonwealth law (Limitation Act periods, the sandbagging position, Privacy Act NDB timing and penalties, payroll tax and superannuation rates, and ATO amendment periods) should be confirmed by NSW counsel against current legislation before they are relied on in negotiation.
- The privacy assessment is time-sensitive. If the Company became aware of the incident some time ago, the NDB assessment clock may already be running, and that should be raised with the deal team and privacy counsel immediately.
